PART 01 — ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

AI Industry Headlines

Aug 3 – Aug 5, 2026 · Funding & M&A · Model Progress · Breakthroughs · Policy

01

Google Launches AI Futures Fund for DeepMind Ecosystem StartupsECOSYSTEM

Google officially launched the AI Futures Fund on August 5, focused on investing in startups leveraging DeepMind's latest AI tools. The fund offers early model access, collaboration with Google experts, and Google Cloud credits. Operating on a rolling basis with no fixed application window, it has already backed startups including Viggle and Toonsutra. This follows Google's Gemma open-source series as another key move to build its AI ecosystem moat.[1]

02

xAI Closes $10B Funding Round, Valuation Rises to $80BFUNDING

Elon Musk's xAI has closed a landmark $10 billion funding round — a mix of equity and debt — to expand AI infrastructure, upgrade the Grok platform, build new data centers, and develop custom AI chips. The round includes roughly $4.3B in equity and $5B in debt financing. Cumulative funding since its 2023 inception now exceeds $24B, pushing valuation from $51B to $80B. xAI is positioning itself as a serious contender against OpenAI.[2]

03

Meta Invests $14.3B for 49% Stake in Scale AI, Superintelligence PushM&A

Meta announced a $14.3 billion strategic investment in Scale AI, acquiring a 49% stake while keeping Scale partially independent. The deal is a major step in Meta's superintelligence strategy — Scale AI is a leader in data labeling and AI training infrastructure. This week also saw Meta expanding AI infrastructure at scale, with capital expenditure guidance continuing to rise.[3]

04

Horizon3 Raises $250M Series E at $2B+ ValuationCYBERSECURITY

Cybersecurity startup Horizon3 has raised $250 million in Series E funding at a valuation exceeding $2 billion — more than tripling in roughly 14 months. The round was led by NightDragon and NEA with existing investors participating. Horizon3 focuses on autonomous AI penetration testing, helping enterprises identify exploitable weaknesses before attackers do. AI-driven cybersecurity continues to attract massive capital.[4]

05

Anthropic-Backed Enterprise Automation Startup Ode Launches Out of StealthAGENTS

Enterprise automation startup Ode, backed by Anthropic, has launched out of stealth with a platform of autonomous domain-specific AI agents designed to replace traditional business process outsourcing (BPO). Built directly on top of Anthropic's advanced reasoning models, Ode's agents execute complex cross-departmental operations — from compliance auditing to supply chain reconciliation — without manual rule programming or rigid visual flowcharts.[5]

06

DeepSeek V4-Flash Named Cheapest Major Model to RunBENCHMARK

Independent benchmarking firm Artificial Analysis reports that DeepSeek V4-Flash is now the cheapest well-known large language model to run — completing its full intelligence-index benchmark suite for roughly 3 US cents. Released August 1, 2026, the model features a 284B total / 13B active MoE architecture with 1M context window. Pricing is roughly 1/100th of comparable Claude models, continuing to put price pressure on international players.[6]

07

Encore AI Secures $30M Series A for Learning Customer Service AgentsFUNDING

Israeli startup Encore AI has closed a $30 million Series A round led by Team8 with participation from Planven and other institutions. The company specializes in analyzing enterprise customer conversation data, training and deploying intelligent voice agents that can operate independently or assist teams. Founded in 2022, the company previously built recommendation software for financial advisors before pivoting fully to enterprise AI customer service.[7]

08

Top 4 US Cloud Firms Spend $730B+ on AI, On Track for $1T by 2027INFRASTRUCTURE

Research shows Google has locked in $200 billion for AI data centers and compute in 2026, with plans to increase further in 2027. Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta have all raised full-year capex guidance. Combined annual AI investment by the four top US cloud companies now exceeds $730 billion, on track to cross the $1 trillion threshold in 2027. All six major tech companies are comprehensively restructuring their supply chains to support the compute buildout.[8]

PART 02 — WEB3 & BLOCKCHAIN

Web3 & Blockchain Headlines

Aug 3 – Aug 5, 2026 · Market Structure · Funding & M&A · Regulation · Security

09

BTC Holds $64K, Fear & Greed Index Rises to 27MARKET

As of August 5, BTC trades at $64,124 (+0.6%), firmly holding the $64K level. Total global crypto market cap is approximately $2.32T. DeFi market cap stands at $61.4B (+1%) with $31.7B in trading volume. The Fear & Greed Index has risen from 25 (Extreme Fear) yesterday to 27 (Fear) — a marginal improvement but still cautious. BTC correlation with US equities has risen to 89%.[9]

10

Cysic Token Surges 93% in a Day, ZK Hardware Heats UpZK HARDWARE

Cysic's CYS token surged 93% in a single day, making it one of the top-performing crypto assets. Cysic is a zero-knowledge hardware acceleration startup that provides hardware acceleration solutions for ZK proof protocols. Within two months of launch, the team developed an FPGA prototype for multi-scalar multiplication (MSM), a key component of ZK protocols. The company raised $18M in prior funding, with ~483M tokens in circulating supply.[10]

11

US and UK Reaffirm Support for Stablecoins and TokenizationREGULATION

The US and UK reaffirmed their support for stablecoins and tokenization during financial regulatory talks on July 8, emphasizing implementation of the GENIUS Act, payment modernization, and cross-border cooperation. The two nations will coordinate more closely on digital asset regulation to balance payment innovation with financial stability. Meanwhile, Ripple is building issuance, stablecoin, trading, custody, and credit infrastructure as institutional tokenization adoption accelerates.[11]

12

CLARITY Act Deadlock Continues, Lummis Urges Dems to End HoldREGULATION

The US CLARITY Act remains stalled in the Senate. A revised 600+ page draft has been introduced, but Democrats continue to block progress. Senator Cynthia Lummis has publicly called on Democrats to stop holding up the bill, with Cathie Wood's Ark Invest also pushing for passage. Key provisions include a three-tier digital asset classification (CFTC commodity / SEC security / GENIUS payment stablecoin), ETP grandfather clauses, and DeFi decentralization tests. Passage before the August recess remains uncertain.[12]

13

Dragonfly Partner: $2 AI Audit Could Have Caught Coldcard FlawSECURITY

Dragonfly Capital partner Haseeb Qureshi argued that a $2 AI audit could have discovered the Coldcard hardware wallet vulnerability. The Coldcard incident has now resulted in losses exceeding 1,800 BTC (~$115M). The root cause was a 2021 firmware version that used a predictable software random number generator instead of the hardware RNG for mnemonic generation. AI-driven smart contract and hardware security auditing is emerging as a new paradigm in on-chain security.[13]

3-Day Outlook

AI side: The capital race enters a new "arms race" phase, with ecosystem building and infrastructure investment advancing on dual fronts. xAI's $10B raise, Meta's $14.3B Scale AI investment, and the $730B+ annual AI spend by the four top cloud firms — the biggest players are pouring into compute and data infrastructure at an unprecedented pace. Meanwhile, Google's AI Futures Fund for ecosystem building, DeepSeek's relentless price pressure, and the tripling of cybersecurity AI valuations like Horizon3 show that the entire value chain, from chips to applications, is undergoing capital-driven accelerated restructuring. Notably, the AI security sector's rise reflects rapidly deepening industry awareness of AI security risks.

Web3 side: Market sentiment is marginally improving, but regulatory uncertainty remains the biggest headwind. BTC's modest rebound from extreme fear and the Cysic token's doubling demonstrate heat in niche sectors like ZK hardware. Yet the CLARITY Act's continued stalemate and the approaching August recess mean policy uncertainty will persist. Structural positives — US-UK stablecoin support, Ripple's institutional infrastructure buildout — continue to accumulate, but the market needs clearer regulatory signals for a larger rally. The Coldcard incident's AI audit discussion, meanwhile, signals that the AI-Web3 intersection is shifting from "growth narrative" to "security necessity."
